info.text:
Is 1/10 of the floor area really enough window? ☀️

New free tool: Daylight Factor.
Enter the room size, window, glass and how high the building opposite is. It works out the average daylight factor, compares it with the target for the room and tells you how wide the window needs to be, with a live section and plan.

✅ BRE average daylight factor method, every step shown
✅ IS 2440 / SP 41 targets (and UK targets)
✅ NBC 2016 window-to-floor check by climate

info.text:
Window = 1/10 of the floor? ❌

In this 4 × 6 m office that gives just 1.41% daylight. An office needs 1.9%: widen the window from 2.0 to 2.7 m ✅

Daylight Factor works out the average daylight factor from the room, glass and what's outside, and tells you how wide the window should be. Free, no sign-up, works offline.

info.text:
How long is a ramp for a 900 mm rise? ♿

New free tool: Accessible Ramp.
Enter the level difference and gradient. It splits the rise into runs, adds every landing, and gives the total length and the plan footprint for a straight or switchback ramp, with a live section and plan.

✅ ADA 2010 limits built in (1:12, 760 mm per run, 1525 mm landings)
✅ UK Part M sliding scale, or enter your local code
✅ Run schedule with levels for your drawings

✅ Wet to dry mortar (× 1.27), bags and cft

How many tiles does this room really need? 🟫

New free tool: Floor Tile Layout.
Enter the room and tile size. It lays out every tile (straight, offset or diagonal), counts the full and cut tiles, flags thin slivers at the walls and gives boxes, skirting and grout.

✅ Tile-by-tile count, not just area + 10%
✅ Centred layout for balanced cuts, or shift the grid yourself
✅ Boxes, skirting tiles and grout in kg

✅ Optional stilt parking and road-width height rule
✅ Floor-by-floor areas in m² and sq ft
